title: If your loved one goes missing
summary: Search for up to 15 minutes, then call 911.
callNow: You've searched for 15 minutes and haven't found them
Your loved one may be in danger right now: near traffic or water, in bad weather, or without needed medicine

steps.title: Start looking right away
steps.text: Don't wait to see if your loved one comes back. Check the home first: closets, the garage, the yard, the car.

steps.title: Search nearby, in the likely direction
steps.text: Many people who wander are found within about 1.5 miles of where they were last seen. Look along the way to places they talks about: an old home, a former job, a church, a favorite store.

steps.title: After 15 minutes, call 911
steps.text: Say: "A person with dementia is missing. They is a vulnerable adult." Police usually don't need to wait 24 hours in this case.

steps.title: Have the details ready
steps.text: A recent photo, height, weight, what they was wearing, where they was last seen, and any medicines they needs.

steps.title: Ask for help
steps.text: Call neighbors and family. If you need help being taken seriously, the Alzheimer's Association 24/7 Helpline can talk with responders.

then: When your loved one is found, stay calm and warm. Don't scold; they may be frightened.
If they was out in heat or cold, or seems hurt or more confused than usual, get medical help.
Afterwards, make a plan: a recent photo on your phone, a list of likely places, ID jewelry or a wandering response service, and a note to neighbors.
dont: Don't wait more than 15 minutes to call 911.
Don't search alone for long: call others in.

sources.name: Alzheimer's Association, wandering and emergency preparedness
